Subject: Prompt set collection & model-fit follow-up — Acme Corp

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the Acme team and see the workflows you outlined for support triage and post-sale automation. Quick recap and the items we discussed: 

- Goal: evaluate model fit for the customer-facing triage assistant (short summaries + action suggestion).
- Desired SLO: 95th percentile latency < 300ms for single-turn queries, and conservative hallucination threshold for action suggestions.
- Initial scope: 5k representative prompts across product search, billing questions, and escalation triage.

Next steps / asks from your side (helps us build the prompt set and run model-fit evals):

1) Export ~200–500 real example prompts per category (CSV preferred). Include: raw user text, any expected redactions, and an example desired assistant output.
2) Flag edge cases — ambiguous requests, multi-intent messages, and examples with PII that require redaction. If you have a redaction guidance doc, please include it.
3) Note any hard constraints (e.g., never expose order numbers in replies).

On our side we'll:
- Run a quick benchmark against recommended models and send a model-fit summary with suggested prompt templates and redaction checks. Recommended starting models (based on throughput/cost/quality tradeoffs):
  - redwood-neo-2.7b (balanced latency + accuracy)
  - redwood-neo-7b-q4 (better quality for long-context summaries)
  - open-llama-7b-quant (cost-efficient baseline)

- Share a link to the benchmark results and a short prompt set template for redaction tagging.

If you can drop the CSV and any redaction policy by EOD Thursday (your timezone), we can run a first-pass evaluation early next week. Happy to do a 30-min technical deep-dive with Rishi/Neha if helpful.

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — reviewed the CSV briefly and ran a quick smoke pass against redwood-neo-2.7b and redwood-neo-7b-q4 on a 128-token budget. High-level takeaways:

- redwood-neo-7b-q4 shows noticeably better instruction following on multi-intent prompts and reduces incorrect action suggestions by ~12% vs 2.7b on the sampled set.
- Latency: 2.7b consistently hits our <300ms target on dedicated infra; 7b-q4 is ~1.6x slower but still close to your SLO on provisioned Dedicated.
- We flagged ~22 examples where expected_output included structured identifiers (order numbers). Recommend pre-redacting those fields and returning a canonical token ("[REDACTED_ORDER]") in both eval and served responses.

Next steps we propose:
1) Run a full 5k prompt sweep on both models and produce the quantitative metrics (accuracy of suggested action, hallucination rate measured by anchor-checks, latency P50/P95).
2) Add a redaction pass to the eval pipeline (pre-redact + keep a mapping for audit). We'll attach a short guidance doc: acme_pii_redaction_guidance.docx.
3) If Acme is comfortable, run a short A/B of instruction-tuned prompt templates that emphasize "do not invent order numbers; ask for confirmation" — early tests often reduce hallucinations for action suggestions.

I'll take ownership of the benchmark run and aim to share a model-fit summary by Friday EOD PT. Neha — can you draft the redaction guidance and provide sample prompt-template transforms?

Samir / Priya — would you be available for the 30-min deep-dive Thursday 10am PT? If not, please propose an alternate.

Cheers,
Rishi
